story:
The Nedat, the downward ones, kept the holy halls of Trollheim and the mound at its root. They carried the dead down the spiral stair and carried the living's questions down after them. Their leader, the Valkyn say, sat at the foot of the mound. That is the Valkyn's way of putting it, and the trolls of Dyrfjall correct them: the Nedat leader did not sit anywhere. It hung.

It hangs still, in the eastern halls, a little way from the Uppat leader, where the roof of the city comes down in long stone teeth. It is the greatest of the stones that hang, and the lesser ones around it hang with it. The trolls say the Fathers found the two great stones together when they first dug the east, one growing up from the floor and one reaching down from the roof, and that the two had not yet met and never would, and that this was the whole of what the Fathers believed about the world: the living go up and the dead go down and the middle is where you stand. They made the bridge over the chasm the boundary between the orders, and they met once a year in the middle of it, and neither set foot on the other's side.

The order that kept the dead took its name from the stone that reaches down. The Nedat keepers who went down to the mound, Grimsa the Downward the last of them, did not take the stone with them; it cannot be carried, and it was never theirs. It stayed in the east when the holy halls emptied, and when the thing came down onto the mound and lay there, it stayed too.

The morvalt leave it alone, and it leaves them alone, which is the only peace in Trollheim. The stalactites around it are less patient, and the Valkyn guides who bring Midgard's scouts that far stop at the edge of them. Those who have gone on and struck the great one say it does not hurry and does not need to. The Valkyn say it has been reaching for the floor since before the trolls went out into the light, and will go on reaching when they have all come home.
legend: Nedat gungledar is a level 70 stone creature in Trollheim's eastern halls, about 2,900 units from Uppat gungledar, hanging among eleven aggressive stalactites (54-56). The leader itself is passive (aggro 0) with no faction, so it never comes unless you hit it and never brings friends. Clear the stalactites first, they're the real hazard on the walk. No special abilities, no quest need; people kill it because it's there and because it's a 70. Don't confuse it with anything to do with Nosdoden: the mound is far to the north. Bring a group that can handle a 70's hits; it has plenty of health and nothing clever.

aggro: You struck the hanging stone. The roof remembers.
The dead go down. You first.
death: The floor... I never touched it...

loremasterTopic.text: The greatest of the hanging stones in the eastern halls, from which the downward order that kept the [mound] took its name. It never sat; it hangs. See [Uppat leader] and [Uppat and Nedat].

bookPage: From what Ivrik the kobold lamp-carrier of Bjarken told the skalds: my grandmother said the kobolds are the children of the Nedat and the trolls of the Uppat, and that is why we go into small dark places and they go up into the light. The trolls laugh at that. But when I stood under the Nedat leader with my lamp out, I felt it the way you feel a parent standing over a bed, and when the Valkyn guide said it was time to go, I went backwards, as you do from a jarl. She did not laugh. She went backwards too.
